messages:
Alex Rivera: ran a focused nsys trace on commit abc123, reproduces the latency bump. timeline shows a kernel-selection flip for the matmul path around t=42s, aten_gemm picked over our small-batch kernel.

Priya Nair: ugh. any idea why selector chose aten_gemm? batch size distribution hasn't changed in the benchmark, right?

Alex Rivera: batch sizes in the trace are 1-4 (mostly 1). kernel selector's scoring pushed aten_gemm because of an outdated throughput heuristic that rewards fused GEMM for longer sequences. sequence len skew seems to have drifted upward for some profiles so selector favours that path.

Mateo Lopez: can you paste the kernel timeline snippet? even a small sample helps.

Alex Rivera: pasted below (nsys capture timeline excerpt):
```
[42.12s] NVTX_RANGE: request_start req=0x7fa3c id=r123
[42.13s] NVTX_RANGE: batch->choose_kernel(seq=128)
[42.1302s] aten_gemm <<< kernel start (12.4ms)
[42.1426s] aten_gemm >>> kernel end
[42.1427s] kv_prefetch(span)
[42.1430s] fallback: small_batch_matmul <<< kernel start (2.1ms)
```
Note: the selector actually launched two kernels for the same logical op due to a late-fallback path.

Casey Wu: that double-launch is nasty. sounds like a race in the timeout/estimation logic?

Jin Park: also NVTX ranges here are a little noisy. we're mixing per-request ranges with fine-grained per-kernel ranges. makes the timeline hard to read. we should standardize a naming scheme.

Samir Rao: +1 on naming. I suggest we adopt a compact, parseable naming convention: "r:{req}|b:{batch}|k:{kernel_short}|s:{seq}". keeps it short and machine-friendly for perf aggregation.

Maya Chen: agree, but watch PII: don't put full request ids or model inputs in ranges. mask or hash req ids. also NVTX has a tiny overhead per range, so avoid adding spans for micro ops.

Priya Nair: proposed levels: level=0 request boundary only, level=1 request + batch boundary, level=2 request+batch+kernel. runtime flag to control. default to 1 in prod.

Alex Rivera: we measured overhead: adding ~2-3 NVTX spans per request (~request start/end + batch) adds ~0.6% median latency. level=2 adds ~2.1% for small-batch workloads. acceptable for debug but not default.

Mateo Lopez: actionable items: 1) fix selector scoring so small-batch path is preferred when batch_size <= 4 and seq <= 64; 2) add a short-circuit to avoid launching fallback kernel if early estimate indicates high probability of success; 3) update NVTX naming and levels.

Jin Park: for naming, I propose exact format: "r:<hash(req)>|b:<bid>|k:<tag>|q:<heuristic>". where <tag> is short id from kernel registry (e.g., km_small, km_gemm), <heuristic> is score bucket (e.g., lowlat, thpt). example: "r:3a7f|b:2|k:km_small|q:lowlat".

Casey Wu: that looks good. we'll need a small lookup table in the perf dashboard to expand kernel tags.

Samir Rao: about sampling: let's push perfetto sampling overlays for long traces and use nsys for short, deterministic captures. when replicating the reg locally, run nsys with --sampling=nvtx to correlate ranges.

Alex Rivera: here's the env config I used to toggle spans in the runtime:
```bash
REDWOOD_NVTX_LEVEL=2 \  # 0/1/2
REDWOOD_NVTX_MASK=kernel,request,batch
REDWOOD_NVTX_HASH_REQ=1
```
Works fine. will push a small patch to guard expensive spans behind level > 0.

Priya Nair: we should also log kernel selection decisions to the trace as attributes (score, time_est, fallback_reason). small JSON blob in NVTX message is ok but keep it <256 bytes.

Maya Chen: careful about JSON in NVTX: some viewers don't render it and large payloads bloat traces. I'd rather have a fixed CSV-ish payload: "score=12|est=1.2ms|fb=none".

Jin Park: agreed. also add a sampling mode that injects a short synthetic request-id into the trace so we can correlate GPU-side events with higher-level spans without exposing real IDs.

Mateo Lopez: for the selector fix, I'm going to open a PR that changes the scoring weights: +15 for small-batch latency preference, -10 for throughput when batch <= 4. will add unit tests and perf test.

Casey Wu: can someone run a perf job before merging? specifically: run perf run-case small-batch (1-4) across the last 10 commits and validate p95 doesn't regress.

Samir Rao: I'll queue the perf job. also will add a dashboard tile that maps NVTX kernel tags to median latency so we can spot regressions quickly.

Alex Rivera: thanks everyone. I'll send a short RFC for the NVTX naming and level flags and link the nsys trace in the PR.

perf-bot: queued perf job #4523: small-batch matrix multiply sweep on commit abc123 -> baseline comparison started. ETA ~25m :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Priya Nair: SGTM. if perf passes, let's merge and roll canary.

Maya Chen: please include a note about masking request ids in the RFC.

Alex Rivera: will do. end of thread. :)
